short.q: Describe the structure and function of a ligament.
short.model: A ligament is a tough band of tissue that joins bone to bone. It stabilises the joint and prevents dislocation.

short.q: Name the type of joint at the knee and the two movements it allows, with a sporting example.
short.model: The knee is a hinge joint allowing flexion and extension, e.g. bending the knee when running and straightening it to kick.

short.q: Explain why weight-bearing exercise is good for the skeleton.
short.model: It makes bones denser and stronger, reducing the risk of osteoporosis, and strengthens ligaments and tendons.
points: lower risk of osteoporosis or injury

short.q: A gymnast does a cartwheel. Name the movement at the shoulder as her arms go out sideways away from the body.
short.model: Abduction at the shoulder, a ball and socket joint, moves the arm away from the midline.

short.q: Give two ways the skeleton helps a rugby player.
short.model: Ribs protect the heart and lungs in tackles; bones act as levers so muscles can move the body to run and pass.
